QTL Analyses via Integrated Modelling

Source: R/qtlAim.R
qtlAim.Rd

Performs forward-selection QTL detection in biparental mapping populations using the whole-genome average interval mapping (wgAim) algorithm of Verbyla et al. (2007, 2012), implemented through the ASReml-R linear mixed modelling engine. All marker intervals or markers are included simultaneously as a composite genome-wide random effect; at each iteration the interval with the highest outlier statistic is nominated as a candidate QTL and tested for significance via a likelihood ratio test (LRT). Significant QTL are added as fixed or random effects and the process repeats until no further significant QTL are detected.

Usage

qtlAim(baseModel, ...)

# Default S3 method
qtlAim(baseModel, ...)

# S3 method for class 'asreml'
qtlAim(
  baseModel,
  genObj,
  merge.by = NULL,
  fix.lines = TRUE,
  gen.type = NULL,
  method = "fixed",
  selection = "interval",
  force = FALSE,
  exclusion.window = 20,
  breakout = -1,
  TypeI = 0.05,
  trace = TRUE,
  verboseLev = 0,
  Trait = NULL,
  str = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

baseModel

A converged asreml model object representing the null model (no QTL effects). Must include the genetic line term in the random formula. If the model has not converged, a single update attempt is made automatically before proceeding.

...

Additional arguments passed to all internal update.asreml calls, such as na.action = na.method(x = "include") or maxit.

genObj

An object of class "wgCross" produced by primeCross. Contains per-chromosome interval midpoint data ($interval.data) and imputed marker data ($imputed.data) used according to gen.type.

merge.by

Character string naming the column present in both the phenotypic data (extracted from baseModel) and genObj that links lines across the two datasets. This is typically the genetic line identifier (e.g. "Genotype").

fix.lines

Logical. If TRUE (default), lines present in the phenotypic data but absent from genObj are accommodated by adding a fixed factor (Gomit) to the model and restricting the genetic random effect to genotyped lines only (Gsave). This ensures that additive and non-additive genetic variance components are estimated from genotyped lines only, avoiding confounding with ungenotyped lines. A harmless warning from ASReml about zero-df terms may appear and can be ignored.

gen.type

Character string, either "interval" (default) or "marker". Controls whether interval midpoint scores ($interval.data) or imputed marker scores ($imputed.data) are used to construct the genome-wide covariate matrix. Interval midpoints are recommended for biparental populations as they better represent the genetic content between flanking markers.

method

Character string, either "fixed" (default) or "random". Determines how detected QTL are incorporated into subsequent iterations. Under "fixed" each QTL is added as an additive fixed effect (Verbyla et al. 2007). Under "random" each QTL is added as an additive random effect with its own variance component (Verbyla et al. 2012). The "random" approach is recommended for populations with many QTL and limited replication as it borrows strength across QTL through shrinkage.

selection

Character string, either "interval" (default) or "chromosome". Under "interval" the interval with the globally highest outlier statistic is selected at each iteration. Under "chromosome" a chromosome-level aggregated outlier statistic is first computed and the best chromosome is selected; the interval with the highest statistic within that chromosome is then chosen. The "chromosome" option is known to perform poorly when chromosomes have few markers and is not recommended in that case.

force

Logical. If FALSE (default), the algorithm automatically selects the vm path (genomic relationship matrix, via vm() in ASReml) when the number of intervals exceeds the number of genotyped lines, and the mbf path (marker-by-file, via mbf() in ASReml) otherwise. If TRUE, the mbf path is forced regardless of the markers-to-lines ratio. The vm and mbf paths are statistically equivalent but differ numerically; the mbf path is more efficient when lines exceed markers.

exclusion.window

Numeric scalar giving the distance in centimorgans on each side of a detected QTL within which further intervals are excluded from selection in subsequent iterations. Default is 20 cM. This prevents selecting multiple intervals within a single QTL region in the same iteration step. Increasing this value leads to more conservative spacing between detected QTL.

breakout

Integer. If set to a positive integer \(n\), the algorithm terminates after \(n\) iterations regardless of significance, returning diagnostic information for those \(n\) iterations but without adding the \(n\)-th QTL as a fixed or random effect. This is useful for inspecting outlier statistics or BLUPs from early iterations. Default is -1 (run to completion).

TypeI

Numeric scalar giving the significance level for the likelihood ratio test used to determine whether a nominated interval is a significant QTL. Default is 0.05. The LRT tests the additive variance parameter of the composite genome-wide term (not an individual interval effect), so this threshold operates as a family-wise error rate without requiring additional multiple-testing correction.

trace

Logical or character string. If TRUE (default), all ASReml output is printed to the console. If a character string giving a file path, output from all ASReml model fits is redirected to that file (errors, warnings and QTL detection messages still appear on screen). Using trace = "trace.txt" is recommended to reduce console clutter during analyses with many iterations.

verboseLev

Integer, either 0 (default) or 1. At verboseLev = 1 a table of per-interval and per-chromosome outlier statistics is printed to the console at each iteration, in addition to the standard ASReml fitting output. Useful for diagnosing the selection process.

Trait

Character string naming a factor column in the phenotypic data that defines the grouping structure for multivariate analysis. The column may represent trials, environments, sites, treatments, or measured traits — any factor whose levels define the multivariate response (e.g. "Trial", "Environment", "Treatment"). When supplied, a multivariate QTL model is fitted using a mixture chi-squared LRT and Wald test pruning to separate main-effect from group-by-genotype interaction QTL. Default NULL (univariate).

str

Character string controlling the variance structure of the additive genomic term in the multivariate model. NULL (default) mirrors the structure on the residual genetic term in baseModel. Explicit options: "corh", "corgh", "us", "diag", or "fa1", "fa2", etc. for factor-analytic structures. The number of factors must be stated explicitly; str = "fa" alone is an error. Only relevant when Trait is non-NULL.

Value

An object of class c("qtlAim","asreml") – the final fitted ASReml model augmented with a $QTL list containing:

$qtl

Character vector of internal key names of detected QTL (e.g. "Chr.3B.14"), in detection order.

$effects

Named numeric vector of estimated QTL additive effects from the final model.

$veffects

Named numeric vector of estimated variances of those QTL effects.

$method

The method argument used ("fixed" or "random").

$type

The gen.type used ("interval" or "marker").

$selection

The selection argument used.

$TypeI

The significance threshold used for the LRT.

$iterations

Total number of forward-selection iterations performed.

$breakout

Integer; the breakout value passed by the user (-1 means the algorithm ran to completion).

$Trait

The Trait column name for multivariate models; NULL for univariate.

$trait.levels

Character vector of factor levels of Trait; NULL for univariate.

$is.interaction

Logical vector (one entry per detected QTL) indicating whether each QTL is a G\(\times\)E interaction effect (TRUE) or a main effect (FALSE). NULL for univariate models.

$diag

A diagnostic list containing:

$oint

Per-iteration list of named numeric vectors of outlier statistics \(\tilde{q}_i^2/\tilde{v}_i\) for all active intervals.

$ochr

Per-iteration list of chromosome-level aggregated statistics (used when selection = "chromosome").

$blups

Per-iteration list of named numeric vectors of scaled BLUPs \(\tilde{q}_i/\sqrt{|\tilde{v}_i|}\).

$lik

Per-iteration list of LRT components ($baseLogL, $stat, $pvalue, $pass).

$lik.mat

Matrix of LRT statistics across iterations, used by aimTrace.

$coef.list

Per-iteration list of named numeric vectors of cumulative QTL fixed (or random) effect estimates.

$vcoef.list

Per-iteration list of named numeric vectors of cumulative QTL effect variances.

$state

Named integer vector recording which intervals have been selected (1) or are still active (0) at the end of the last iteration.

$genetic.term

Name of the genetic line identifier column used in the model.

$rel.scale

Numeric scaling constant \(s\) used to normalise the genomic relationship matrix \(G = XX'/s\).

Additionally, the updated phenotypic data frame (with QTL genotype columns appended) is assigned to <response>.data in the calling environment.

Details

Algorithm overview:

  1. All marker intervals are assembled into a genome-wide covariate matrix \(M\) (lines x intervals).

  2. An initial genome-wide model is fitted in which all intervals collectively contribute a composite random genetic term (either vm(line, G) or mbf('ints')).

  3. At each iteration, an outlier statistic \(\tilde{q}_i^2 / \tilde{v}_i\) is computed for every active interval \(i\), where \(\tilde{q}_i\) is the back-transformed conditional BLUP of the interval effect and \(\tilde{v}_i\) is its posterior variance. The interval with the maximum outlier statistic is nominated.

  4. A likelihood ratio test (LRT) is performed: \(2(\ell_1 - \ell_0) \sim \chi^2_1\), testing whether the composite genome-wide additive variance parameter is zero. If the one-sided p-value \(< TypeI\), the nominated interval is a significant QTL.

  5. The selected QTL is added to the model as a fixed or random effect (according to method), the composite genome-wide term is rebuilt excluding the selected interval and any intervals within exclusion.window cM, and the process repeats.

vm vs mbf path: The vm path builds a genomic relationship matrix \(G = XX'/s\) (where \(s\) is a scaling constant) and fits vm(line, G) in ASReml. The mbf path passes the interval matrix directly to ASReml via mbf('ints') and is equivalent but more efficient when lines \(\ge\) markers. Both paths produce identical QTL selections.

References

Verbyla, A.P., Cullis, B.R. and Thompson, R. (2007). The analysis of QTL by simultaneous use of the full linkage map. Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 116, 95–111.

Verbyla, A.P., Taylor, J.D. and Verbyla, K.L. (2012). RWGAIM: An efficient high-dimensional random whole genome average (QTL) interval mapping approach. Genetics Research, 94, 291–306.

See also

summary.qtlAim, print.qtlAim, aimTrace, linkMap.qtlAim, primeCross, gwasAim, gpAim

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(asreml)
data(phenoRxK, package = "wgAim")
data(genoRxK,  package = "wgAim")

# Prepare wgCross object
genoRxK <- subset(genoRxK, chr = c("1A","2D1","2D2","3B"))
genoRxK <- primeCross(genoRxK, impute = "Martinez", id = "Genotype")

# Fit null base model
base.mod <- asreml(yld ~ Type + lrow,
                   random   = ~ Genotype + Range,
                   residual = ~ ar1(Range):ar1(Row),
                   data     = phenoRxK)

# Forward-selection QTL analysis
qtl.fit <- qtlAim(base.mod, genObj = genoRxK,
                  merge.by = "Genotype",
                  trace    = "trace.txt",
                  na.action = na.method(x = "include"))

# Results
print(qtl.fit,   genObj = genoRxK)
summary(qtl.fit, genObj = genoRxK)
aimTrace(qtl.fit)
linkMap(qtl.fit, genObj = genoRxK)
} # }
